text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- President Jacques Chirac dissolved the National Assembly yesterday and called an early parliamentary election for May 25 and June 1, saying France needed to join a single currency from a position of strength. He wanted the French people to "express themselves clearly on the scale and speed of change over the next five years", calling for a reform of the state and cuts in public spending and taxes. (Les Echos, La Tribune, L'Agefi, Le Figaro, Liberation, The International Herald Tribune).
LES ECHOS
-- Right-wing politicians hail Chirac's decision to hold an early election, while left-wing predicts further austerity.
-- Consumption proved disappointing in March for the second consecutive month.
-- Plan to reduce automobile traffic in Paris on days of heavy air pollution to be implemented from today.
-- U.S. film studio Warner Bros, to buy a 10 percent stake in CanalSatellite.
-- Airbus chairman of supervisory board Edzard Reuter threatens to resign if consortium's move to limited company status is jeopardised.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Only 28 percent of professionals recommend investing on the Paris bourse in view of uncertainty on French politics and on U.S. rates.
-- The mark rose against the franc yesterday to 3.3740.
-- Prices of paper pulp expected to rise by May 1.

-- Spanish telecommunications minister Rafael Arias Salgado says in an interview he favours a gradual deregulation of telecommunications, and opposes some of Canal Plus points of view on grounds they may distort fair competition in the digital TV market.
-- Social Security bank Acoss confirms its forecast of 35.2 billion francs cash deficit for 1997.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Politicians divided over how to steer the economy toward growth needed for France to bring public deficit in line with Maastricht criteria.
-- Consumer spending by people over 50 expected to account for half of French society's overall income by the year 2005, study shows.
-- Alcatel Alsthom sells Medoc vineyard Gruau Larose to Bernard Taillans Vins.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- New-Caledonia separatists continue to block exports of nickel from Eramet subsidiary SLN.
-- Negotiations between unions and management at British Airways subsidiaries TAT-Air Liberte carry on.

-- Paribas chairman Andre Levy-Lang says in an interview the bank intends to strengthen its position in Asia and notably in China and on financial markets, is about to buy Hong-Kong-based broker Asia Equity Holdings for some 300 million francs.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Decision to call early election in France could turn French political preferences into a decisive referendum on Europe's single currency project, officials and analysts warn.
